newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee harvest gathers pace, prices steady.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee harvest gathers pace, prices steady.

text.p: A let-up in heavy rains allowed harvesting and drying to resume in Vietnam's main coffee-growing region, Dak Lak province, traders said on Friday.

"We had a week of sunshine, and that brought a lot of coffee out onto the roads for drying," said one trader, who estimated that up to 15 percent of Dak Lak's 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) robusta crop had now been harvested.

However, a tropical depression brought rain again on Friday morning, which traders said could hamper drying and cause quality problems. One trader put the moisture levels in the beans he was buying at about 16.5 percent.
"That's about normal," he said. "Sixteen-and-a-half is high, but it's not horribly, unacceptably high."

Traders said the more clement weather had cut transport problems and helped lift shipments. On Wednesday they estimated the amount of beans sold and shipped by Vietnam in the past week at between 5,000 and 10,000 tonnes compared with just a few hundred tonnes a week earlier.
Export prices were little changed, shadowing the sideways trend on terminal markets. Traders quoted a price of $1,090-1,100 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, about $10 lower than a week ago.
